dielectric_constant.interpretation: Lower dielectric constant → Higher conductivity (confounded by viscosity)

cross_property_hypotheses.hypothesis: Solvents with larger HOMO-LUMO gaps enable higher ionic conductivity
cross_property_hypotheses.evidence: DMC (gap=9.0 eV) has avg σ=9.78 mS/cm vs PC (gap=7.9 eV) with σ=3.45 mS/cm
cross_property_hypotheses.mechanism: Larger electrochemical window reduces side reactions, improving ion transport

cross_property_hypotheses.hypothesis: Low-viscosity linear carbonates (DMC, EMC, DEC) enable higher conductivity than cyclic carbonates (EC, PC)
cross_property_hypotheses.evidence: DMC: σ=9.78 mS/cm, EMC: σ=5.44 mS/cm vs EC: σ=5.25 mS/cm, PC: σ=3.45 mS/cm
cross_property_hypotheses.mechanism: Lower viscosity improves ion mobility despite lower dielectric constant

cross_property_hypotheses.hypothesis: Solvents with higher LUMO energy (>0 eV) provide better conductivity
cross_property_hypotheses.evidence: DMC (LUMO=+0.2 eV): σ=9.78 mS/cm vs EC (LUMO=-0.4 eV): σ=5.25 mS/cm
cross_property_hypotheses.mechanism: Higher LUMO indicates greater reduction stability

cross_property_hypotheses.hypothesis: FEC additive reduces conductivity but improves SEI formation
cross_property_hypotheses.evidence: FEC formulations: avg σ=4.16 mS/cm (lower than EC-only), but LUMO=-0.8 eV (most reducible)
cross_property_hypotheses.mechanism: FEC preferentially reduces to form protective SEI layer

top_patterns: EC + PC + EMC is the most common solvent combination
LiPF6 is present in >90% of high-conductivity formulations
Acetonitrile and DMSO enable highest single-solvent conductivity
